issue_context.title: Setting MSAA to 1 sample to disable it is really confusing
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

It's confusing that you have to set the `samples` value to 1 to turn off MSAA.

## What solution would you like?

Ira presented a pretty good one: https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/1051819150189809715/1051822325907079208 Just have the MSAA be a field on the camera like HDR.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

Could have an MSAA enum like:

```rust
enum MSAA {
    On(u32),
    Off,
}
```

and insert that as a resource.
comments: It always made sense to me, but I guess it assumes a lot of rendering knowledge. I'd approve a PR with this change.

Sample counts can (or at least I have never seen anything else) only be 2^n. But even this rule is limited. In Vulkan there are only the values 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. I don't think anything beyond that would be useful or even supported by any platform. Therefore I would suggest the following MSAA enum:

```
enum MSAA {
    Off,
    Sample2,
    Sample4,
    Sample8,
    Sample16,
    Sample32,
    Sample64
} 
```

As a positive side effect, no invalid values could be provided.
Only 1 and 4 are supported for now: https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/issues/1832
Good point, and as you said this could still change in the future. For this reason I think it makes sense to use `#[non_exhaustive]` and for now only use the available values.

review_comments: Rather than complicate this with two types, maybe it should just be a flat enum? `Msaa::from(MultiSampleLevel::Sample4)` is a mouth full. Why not just `Msaa::Sample1`?
